entities.summary:
Saint Servatius (unknown–384 AD), Bishop of Tongeren, was a significant figure in the early Christian Church.

 A 4th-century bishop and saint, Servatius played a crucial role in the spread of Christianity throughout the Roman Empire. He was a key figure in the development of the Diocese of Tongeren and worked tirelessly to convert the local population to Christianity.

 Servatius's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped establish the Church as a dominant force in Western Europe. His influence can still be felt today, particularly in the region of Flanders, where he is revered as a patron saint.

 The exact circumstances of Servatius's life are shrouded in mystery, but it is clear that he left an indelible mark on the course of Christian history. His feast day, May 13, is still celebrated by Christians around the world, serving as a reminder of his enduring significance.
